newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo says underestimated Coke in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo says underestimated Coke in Brazil.

text.p: Pepsico Inc said on Friday that its international soft drinks operations were hurt by overextending itself in Brazil, where it underestimated rival Coca-Cola Co's strength.

Chief executive Roger Enrico said Latin American Pepsi bottler Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA) "invested too much, too fast" and got caught in an economic downturn and sharp competition, citing in particular Brazil.
"They caught up in a vast and alluring market, Brazil, which seemed better than it actually was for us," Enrico told a telephone conference with industry analysts.
"Coke's very deeply entrenched in that country," he added. "I think it clearly was true that we underestimated Coke's strength in Brazil."

Late Thursday PepsiCo said it expected earnings per share for the third quarter to be about $0.30 below the same period last year, citing an estimated $360 million pre-tax charge to be incurred in its international beverage business. It earned $0.39 a share in 1995's third quarter, accounting for a two-for-one stock split.
Enrico said Pepsi would focus on a "few high opportunity markets" to grow its international beverage sales where the company sees itself on a "a level playing field" with Coke.
He listed India, China, the former Soviet Union and Eastern Europe among potential growth markets.
